newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares end at new highs, more gains seen.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares end at new highs, more gains seen.

text.p: Belgian shares climbed to new highs on Friday, swept upwards with neighbouring markets as Wall Street reacted well to U.S. jobs data, and with no end to the bull run in sight.

"All the things that move the market are positive. Interest rates are still low, the dollar is very positive...," said Stefan Casteleyn, analyst at Corluy and Co. His target for the Bel-20 in 1997 remained at 2,300.
The Bel-20 index .BFX rose 16.90 points or 0.82 percent to end at 2,080.50, after touching an all-time high of 2,086.97. Volume was solid at 3.3 billion francs of Belgian shares.
Top Bel-20 gainer was insurer Royale Belge, climbing sharply for the fourth day in a row to end 410 francs or 5.62 percent higher at 7,710.
Casteleyn noted the share had trailed fellow insurer Belgian-Dutch insurance and banking group Fortis AG and was now catching up.

An article in weekly investment paper Cash! this week also highlighted Royale Belge as a lagger, and speculated about whether Belgian financier Albert Frere might sell GBL's stake in the insurer to French insurer Axa-UAP and want to buy Suez shares from Axa-UAP in return.
"(The rise) is a bit overdone," one dealer said.
Chemical stock Solvay cut most of its early losses to end just 75 francs or 0.3 percent lower at 22,300.
The stock tumbled to 21,725 earlier after the company disappointed the market with its 1996 preliminary profit figures released late on Thursday.
